PROTOCOL TITLE: Sickle Cell Disease Longitudinal Natural History Study and
Biorepository Registry with Embedded Qualitative Patient/Caregiver Experience
Substudy

PROTOCOL NUMBER: SCD-NHS-014
VERSION: 2.1, dated 2026-04-15

1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE
Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a chronic, multi-system genetic hemoglobinopathy
characterized by recurrent vaso-occlusive crises (VOCs), progressive organ
damage, and shortened life expectancy. This is a non-interventional natural
history study combining retrospective chart abstraction, prospective
electronic health record (EHR) linkage, biospecimen banking, patient-reported
outcomes, and a qualitative patient/caregiver experience substudy to
characterize the real-world disease and treatment trajectory across the
lifespan, including patients who have received newly approved gene therapies.

2. STUDY OBJECTIVES
Primary: Characterize the longitudinal burden of VOC frequency, organ
complications, and healthcare utilization in a real-world SCD cohort followed
for up to 15 years, including post-gene-therapy long-term follow-up (LTFU)
participants.
Secondary: Build a linked clinical-genomic-biospecimen biorepository;
characterize patient- and caregiver-reported disease burden; and describe
lived experience of VOC management and gene therapy decision-making through
qualitative interviews.

3. STUDY DESIGN
This is a single-IRB, multi-site (12 academic sickle cell centers),
non-interventional longitudinal cohort study. There is no investigational
product and no randomization. Enrollment target is 2,400 participants across
pediatric and adult sites, with a planned follow-up duration of 15 years to
capture the full FDA-mandated long-term follow-up window for gene-therapy
recipients (insertional oncogenesis and secondary malignancy surveillance).
Design combines four concurrent data-collection modes in one protocol:
(1) retrospective chart abstraction, (2) prospective EHR-linked electronic
data capture, (3) biospecimen collection and long-term biobanking, and
(4) an embedded qualitative substudy — the complex multi-modal design this
checklist's Dimension 6 was written to score.

4. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
Inclusion: Confirmed diagnosis of SCD (HbSS, HbSC, HbS-beta thalassemia) of
any age; willing to provide historical medical records; willing to provide
biospecimens where applicable.
Exclusion: Unwilling to consent to EHR linkage or record retrieval from
outside institutions.

5. RETROSPECTIVE CHART ABSTRACTION
Full lifetime treatment history will be abstracted for each participant,
frequently spanning multiple decades of care. Abstraction is expected to
exceed 500 charts across the 12 participating centers and will require deep
multi-year chart review per patient, including hospitalization records,
transfusion history, hydroxyurea and disease-modifying therapy exposure, and
transplant/gene-therapy records. A substantial fraction of source records are
scanned or unstructured (handwritten emergency department notes, outside
hospital discharge summaries) and will require manual review; outside-record
requests will be needed for approximately 30% of participants who received
care at non-network facilities before enrollment.

6. PROSPECTIVE ELECTRONIC DATA CAPTURE
Each site will establish a continuous, near-real-time electronic data feed
from its EHR into the study's central i2b2/OMOP-based research data
warehouse, capturing laboratory values, hospitalizations, and medication
orders as they occur. This requires dedicated informatics support at each
site, cross-institutional data-use agreements, and ongoing automated
data-quality monitoring for feed interruptions and coding drift.

7. UNSCHEDULED / EVENT-DRIVEN VISIT AND CONTACT BURDEN
Because VOC frequency and severity drive nearly all clinical contact in this
population, the study captures unscheduled, event-triggered visits rather
than a fixed protocol-scheduled visit calendar. Sites must maintain 24/7
on-call capacity to identify, consent, and document participants presenting
to the emergency department or being admitted with an acute VOC, and must
coordinate real-time data capture with after-hours ED and inpatient teams.

8. BIOSPECIMEN COLLECTION AND BIOREPOSITORY
Whole blood, plasma, and buccal/genomic DNA specimens will be collected at
enrollment and at annual follow-up visits. Specimens undergo specialized
processing (PBMC isolation, plasma separation under defined timing windows)
and are stored long-term at -80C and in liquid nitrogen vapor phase with full
chain-of-custody tracking. A subset of specimens will be shared with external
academic and industry biorepositories under material transfer agreements to
support future genomic and biomarker research.

9. PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES
Participants complete an extensive PRO battery: the ASCQ-Me disease-specific
instrument, PROMIS pain interference and fatigue short forms, and a
high-frequency daily electronic pain/symptom diary completed via a
smartphone app for 14-day bursts every quarter. Pediatric participants
complete validated proxy-report versions administered through a caregiver,
and low-literacy accommodations (audio-assisted electronic administration)
are available at all sites.

10. QUALITATIVE PATIENT/CAREGIVER EXPERIENCE SUBSTUDY
A purposively sampled subset of patients, caregivers, and treating clinicians
across all 12 sites will participate in semi-structured interviews and focus
groups exploring VOC self-management, gene therapy decision-making, and
transition from pediatric to adult care. Interviews are audio-recorded,
professionally transcribed, and coded in NVivo using a multi-coder,
consensus-based reliability process with iterative recruitment to thematic
saturation across each stakeholder group; dedicated qualitative-methods staff
oversee the coding process.

11. LONG-TERM FOLLOW-UP FOR GENE THERAPY RECIPIENTS
Participants who have received an FDA-approved gene therapy for SCD are
followed under a 15-year long-term follow-up schedule with sustained
in-person visits and specialized long-term safety monitoring, including
integration-site analysis and ongoing surveillance for secondary
malignancy and insertional oncogenesis, consistent with FDA long-term
follow-up guidance for genetically modified cell therapies.

12. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS
This is a descriptive natural history study; no formal hypothesis testing is
planned for the primary objective. Enrollment of 2,400 participants across 12
sites over a 15-year observation window is expected to provide adequate
precision for estimating VOC incidence rates and complication prevalence
across age strata.

13. REGULATORY AND ANCILLARY REQUIREMENTS
Single IRB of record for all 12 sites. Data-use agreements required between
each site and the coordinating center for EHR linkage. Biorepository
operates under a separate biobanking protocol amendment. No investigational
product is administered under this protocol.
